name: verify-real-outcome
description: Verify the real user-facing outcome after implementation. Use when a task includes a build, release, deployment, browser flow, runtime path, or deliverable that must be proven outside source code.
scenario: An agent finishes after the build passes without exercising the real user-visible workflow.
desiredOutcome: Prove that the implemented change works through the narrowest real user-facing acceptance path
verification: Capture the command, browser flow, runtime observation, or artifact inspection that directly proves the requested outcome
positiveTriggers: Finish the release and verify the installed application
Deploy this change and check the real browser flow
Create the artifact and prove that it opens correctly
negativeTriggers: Explain how our build pipeline works
Review this deployment proposal without changing anything
processSteps: Identify the observable user-facing outcome in the request
Choose the narrowest real runtime path that proves that outcome
Run implementation checks before touching the real acceptance path
Exercise the real path and capture direct evidence
doneCriteria: The tested runtime or artifact corresponds to the implemented source
The handoff names the verification performed and any remaining boundary
